newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures end higher in temporary correction.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures end higher in temporary correction.

text.p: NYCE frozen concentrated orange juice futures retraced some of the sharp losses made Monday and settled firmer in moderate activity.
Floor sources said speculative short-covering and trade buying accounted for most of the day's volume, estimated at a brisk 3,500 lots.
January juice ended 2.20 higher to 91.20, traded 91.90 to 89.60 cents. The back months settled 1.35 to 2.20 higher.
Despite the day's gains, the near-term outlook remains to the downside.
"The charts are still in the negative zone," an analyst said, pegging nearby support at Monday's low of 88.25 basis the January contract.
She said the market remains oversold and could rally another 3.00 to 4.00 cents before running into resistance seen at 93.25 and then at 94.70 basis January.

Players also await Wednesday's spec/hedge report. Last week, the report showed the speculators nearly split at 47 percent long and 42 percent short. Analysts noted that the speculators typically have a much higher net long position at this time of year due to colder temperatures.
But the weather remains mild across the Florida citrus belt with a robust orange crop forecast for the season.

"In terms of the fundamentals, it appears that the market is still focused on the supply side, as there is plenty of juice around, imports continue their active pace, and the new season promises a record crop," Walter Spilka, an analyst with Smith Barney, said in a weekly report.
